div.h1: One secure workplace. One support team. One future-ready organization.
div.p: A customized proposal to modernize employee onboarding, IT support, security, backup, business continuity, communications, and AI readiness for .

div.h2: The next step in a trusted relationship
div.p: Hudson Guild has trusted IPPBX with communications for approximately seven years. This proposal extends that relationship into the broader workplace surrounding those communications.

Based on the preliminary discussion, Hudson Guild's current technology environment appears to rely heavily on traditional, device-by-device support. Employee onboarding may require hands-on configuration of computers, applications, email, phone extensions, voicemail, shared files, permissions, and other workplace tools.

IPPBX recommends replacing that fragmented model with a centrally managed Modern Digital Workplace designed to make employee onboarding faster, support more responsive, security more consistent, and the organization better prepared for future automation and AI.

div.strong: Your office should not live inside one laptop.
div.p: The laptop should become a secure window into the employee's approved workplace: applications, files, communications, permissions, security policies, and support.

div.h2: What this proposal is designed to solve

article.p: Prepare employee access, applications, Google Workspace, phone, voicemail, and permissions before day one.
Deliver remote-first assistance without removing onsite support when physical or hands-on work is required.
Standardize user profiles, security policies, applications, storage, and support instead of rebuilding every computer separately.
Review scattered and duplicated information before migration rather than transferring disorder into a new environment.
Reduce employee dependence on one physical computer and improve recovery when a device fails.
Organize systems, permissions, and workflows now so AI can be introduced responsibly later.

div.p: The solution is designed to centralize employee identity, applications, files, communications, security, backup, support, technology assets, and recovery planning inside one managed operating environment.
Create approved access based on employee role.
Deliver applications, files, communications, and permissions centrally.
Resolve most employee issues without waiting for travel.
Keep hands-on assistance available for physical work.

div.h2: A controlled transition - not a disruptive technology event

article.p: Review users, devices, applications, Google Workspace, storage, security, vendors, and support processes.
Define user profiles, access, storage, application delivery, security, backup, and support procedures.
Test representative employees, common applications, file access, phone tools, printing, and support.
Migrate employees in controlled groups with documentation, support, and post-migration follow-up.
Review support issues, security, backup, asset records, user satisfaction, and the technology roadmap.

div.h2: Security, support, backup, and continuity in one program

article.p: Managed cloud workplace, user profiles, application delivery, file access, remote work, and standard storage policy.
Remote support, login assistance, password help, application access, onboarding, offboarding, and escalation.
Extension creation, voicemail setup, phone onboarding, documentation, and communications support.
Centralized monitoring, alert review, investigation support, incident oversight, and escalation.
Behavior-based detection and managed response beyond conventional signature-based antivirus.
Managed simulations, employee education, training follow-up, participation reporting, and risk trends.
Backup for Gmail, Drive, Chat, Calendar, and Contacts to strengthen recovery beyond native retention.
Track devices, ownership, assigned users, lifecycle status, warranty information, and replacement needs.
Plan equipment replacements, application renewals, security improvements, and technology priorities.
Leadership-ready reporting covering activity, risks, improvements, and areas requiring attention.
Recovery planning, backup coordination, critical-system identification, and employee-access recovery procedures.
Organized systems, clearer permissions, and documented workflows for responsible future automation.

div.p: Most employee support is delivered remotely because it is faster and more efficient. When work is physical, onsite assistance can be scheduled.
Examples include device deployment, office moves, physical troubleshooting, network and cabling assistance, local equipment installation, specialized equipment, and in-person rollout support.
Travel time is billed separately. Hardware, materials, parking, tolls, shipping, and other direct expenses are billed separately when applicable.
